Subject: Questions on EU-only processing assurances and access logging

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal and privacy teams have a few follow-ups before we progress to procurement. High level asks: can Redwood commit to processing BioMedica EU customer data only in EU jurisdictions (no US operator access), provide a standardized artifact proving backup location and deletion windows, and a log entitlement showing operator access events for the last 12 months?

Specifically:
- A firm statement about geographic hosting for both inference and control plane data.
- Whether backups or failover replicas may be stored outside EU and, if so, what controls and safeguards apply.
- Evidence for SCCs/Schrems-II mitigation measures and whether Redwood offers KMS split-key or customer-managed keys in EU.
- The format of the audit log we can expect (fields, retention) and whether we can get a sample extract.

We need this to satisfy internal counsel and the procurement checklist. Can you loop in engineering/privacy and provide a single consolidated response?

Best,
Sara

Hi Sara — copying the legal response here and the commitments we can make in writing. Please consider this a draft that we can convert into contract language if you proceed.

Summary of legal commitments (draft):
1) Data localization: Redwood will route and process BioMedica production inference requests and associated customer data exclusively in EU jurisdictions (AWS eu-west-1, GCP europe-west1, or Azure West Europe), as specified in the order form. Control plane metadata required for routing will also be stored in EU regions.

2) Backups & DR: Redwood will configure backups and disaster recovery replicas to remain within EU regions only; Redwood will not perform automatic replication outside the EU for BioMedica unless explicitly authorized in writing.

3) Operator access & SCCs: Redwood will include the standard SCCs (EU Commission modules) and a supplement limiting operator administrative access to named Redwood operators under role-based access with just-in-time approvals and MFA. Redwood will provide an attestation describing access controls, and an appendix mapping potential legal process (e.g., lawful government requests) and our notification process.

4) KMS options: we offer customer-managed KMS keys with EU-region key material (BYOK) and an alternative split-key arrangement for higher assurance customers.

5) Logging & evidence: Redwood will provide a sample syslog export and a one-time historical extract of operator-access events (up to 12 months) in CSV format, subject to redaction for operator identities where required by internal policy. The sample will include fields: timestamp, action, resource, operator_role, request_id, outcome. We will also provide hash-signed snapshots of deletion operations tied to retention periods.

Next steps: Naomi will attach the technical artifacts (audit sample and hosting commitment PDF). If BioMedica would like contractual language, we can convert items 1–4 into an amendment and run it through legal.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Legal & Compliance | Redwood Inference
From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Sara — attaching the artifacts we promised. See inline answers plus attachments.

Attachment: redwood-eu-hosting-commitment.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: operator-access-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Inline summary of technical answers:
- Hosting & control plane: All production inference workloads and associated model cache/KV data for BioMedica will be pinned to EU-only clusters. Control-plane telemetry used for routing will be stored in the EU control plane instance dedicated to the customer.

- Backups & DR: Backups are stored in encrypted blobs within EU regions; snapshots used for DR are only promoted within EU unless a manual TOC approval is provided. Retention policy: default 30 days for incremental snapshots, 365 days for long-term archival (customer-selectable). We propose BioMedica choose 90-day incremental / 365-day archival for the pilot.

- KMS & keys: We can enable customer-managed keys with key material kept in an EU KMS; BYOK flow documented in the attached PDF. Split-key workflow requires a short operations onboarding (we provide the orchestration; customer retains root share).

- Audit & logs: Sample extract attached (CSV) and the schema is: timestamp, event_type, resource_id, region, operator_role, correlation_id, result, notes. We can provide 12 months of operator-event rows as a one-time export (subject to redaction for operator PII). Ongoing log streaming to a customer-owned S3/GCS (EU bucket) is also supported.

- Schrems-II / SCCs: The SCC modules we use are included in the redline appendix in the PDF. Practical mitigation controls: EU-only placement, customer-managed keys, operator role constraints, and encrypted backups. We will provide a short attestation letter for procurement as part of the amendment.

If this meets your needs I'll have legal prepare an amendment and Jonas can schedule a quick call to agree retention choices and the timing for the one-time log extract.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Privacy Operations | Redwood Inference
